decisions.reason: The same message independently sets the 70×50 board dimensions, which are already captured; retaining individual sensor connectors does not require another form-factor state change.
The connector-consolidation decision does not alter ESP32 antenna placement; the separate edge-placement clause is already represented.
The four-layer choice is an independent clause already captured for this Requirement; retaining individual JST connectors does not change the layer count.
The source preserves individual sensor-module cables but does not change the existing placement, accessibility, or alignment rules for the main-to-sensor interboard connectors.
Keeping separate sensor cables does not entail any change to I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, or cable-length assumptions.
The rejected fan-out proposal concerns consolidation of individual sensor connections and does not change the established main-to-sensor power and signal interfaces.
The SPS30's existing dedicated 1.5 mm connector remains valid unchanged; the source establishes a broader non-consolidation policy without changing its connector type or pinout.
The source discusses sensor-board connector modularity and does not alter power-board connector placement, orientation, or accessibility.
The decision to retain separate sensor cables does not change the inventory or wiring of panel-control connectors.
Connector consolidation has no entailed effect on any documented ESP32-S3 GPIO assignment.
The sensor-connector policy does not alter USB enumeration, programming behavior, connector sourceability, or USB signal routing.
Retaining individual connectors changes wiring organization within the existing sensor-board design but does not change the number or identity of the project's separate boards.
